prae-clŭĕo , ēre, v. n.,
I.to be very famous or renowned (post-class.): “qui in vetustā praecluent comoediā,” Ter. Maur. p. 2433 P.: “praecluens potestas,” Prud. Cath. 4, 37 .—In the collat. form praeclŭo , ĕre, v. n.: “vos, qui ex ubertate terrae praecluatis,” Jul. Val. Rer. Gest. Alex. M. 1, 38 Mai.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
